{{Quote|Poodoo!|Sebulba after crashing his Podracer in the [[Boonta Eve Classic/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]]|<ref name="Episode 1">{{Film|I}}</ref>}}
'''Sebulba''' was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Dug/Legends|Dug]] hailing from the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] planet [[Malastare/Legends|Malastare]]. He was a former [[Slavery/Legends|slave]] who had bought his freedom with his incredible skills at piloting a high-speed [[Podracer/Legends|Podracer]], and the well-known archrival of a young [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Podracer (profession)/Legends|Podracer]] named [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]]. Before long, Sebulba became the star racer of the [[Galactic Podracing Circuit/Legends|Galactic Podracing Circuit]], based not only on his formidable racing skills but also his penchant for violence. Many fellow Podracers were [[Death/Legends|killed]] or injured by Sebulba's reckless steering or out-and-out cheating, but Sebulba was far too popular to be blamed or penalized.

==Biography==
===Early life===
[[File:SebulbaGellaTwinMassage-TPM.png|thumb|left|250px|Sebulba receives a massage from his twin Twi'lek slaves.]]
Sebulba was a [[Dug/Legends|Dug]] from the city of [[Pixelito/Legends|Pixelito]] on the planet [[Malastare/Legends|Malastare]].<ref name="SW 14">[[Star Wars (1998) 14|''Star Wars'' (1998) 14]]</ref> Like most Dugs, Sebulba was belligerent and aggressive, and constantly felt the need to prove his superiority. Despite their camel-like facial structures, Dugs were arboreal, and could use all four of their limbs equally. Sebulba preferred supporting his weight with his arms and performing fine tasks with his legs. While in the seat of a [[Podracer/Legends|Podracer]], however, he used all four limbs, his arms to steer and his legs to manipulate the finer instruments in the pod.

Sebulba spent his earnings on a decadent lifestyle. His most prized possessions included a pair of [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] twin sisters,<ref name="Visual">''[[Star Wars: The Phantom Menace: The Expanded Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> named [[Ann Gella/Legends|Ann]] and [[Tann Gella/Legends|Tann Gella]], who were trained [[Yobana/Legends|masseuses]].<ref name="NEGTC" /> He also owned at least two more female Twi'lek slaves, a [[Rutian/Legends|Rutian]] and a [[Lethan/Legends|Lethan]], who were in [[Sebulba's private apartment|his apartment]] by [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].<ref name="TPM video game">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' video game]]</ref> Sebulba often used his fame for cheap dalliances with Dug females. Sebulba also had his hands in several slaving rings for [[Gardulla Besadii the Elder/Legends|Gardulla the Elder]].<ref name="NEGTC" />

When decked out for a race, Sebulba always looked his finest. On his heavily padded racing suit hung numerous trophy coins, a testament to his success. In order to ensure victory, the wily Dug would stop at nothing. While bribing and flat-out cheating were certainly useful, Sebulba largely preferred either pressing his opponents from the track and into obstacles or using the built-in weapons on his Podracer. He would even try and sabotage other pods when [[Podracer (profession)/Legends|racers]] were not looking. At one time, his vehicle was designed to shoot nails into opponents; later, he poured funds into [[Plug-F Mammoth Split-X engine/Legends|his racer]] to install a [[Flamethrower/Legends|flamethrower]].

===Boonta Eve Classic===
{{Quote|Yoka to Bantha poodoo!|Sebulba to [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]]|<ref name="Episode 1" />}}
[[File:Sebulba.png|thumb|right|250px|Sebulba during the Boonta Eve Classic]]
In 32 BBY, Sebulba was the obvious favorite to win the [[Boonta Eve Classic/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]]. He also got into a fight with [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]] in retaliation for Binks accidentally spitting a [[Gorg/Legends|Gorg]] he attempted to eat after learning of its expensive cost, into Sebulba's soup. However, the local slave boy [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], who was also one of his opponents in the Classic, broke up the fight before it began. Sebulba dismissed his anger at Jar Jar to insult Anakin's chances at Podracing.<ref name="Episode 1" />

Sometime before the race, Sebulba gave a [[Sebulba's secret note to Jabba|secret note]] to a pit droid called [[DUM-4/Legends|DUM-4]], to deliver to [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt]].<ref name="APD">''[[Anakin's Pit Droid]]''</ref> In the first lap, he destroyed [[Mawhonic/Legends|Mawhonic's]] Podracer in the first stretch of the course. In the second lap, he used the illegal flamethrower mounted on his Plug-F ''Mammoth'' to roast [[Clegg Holdfast/Legends|Clegg Holdfast's]] engines, destroying his pod. He also ditched a piece of iron into [[Mars Guo/Legends|Mars Guo's]] giant engine turbines, blowing it up. In addition, he also was targeted by fellow racer [[Ratts Tyerell/Legends|Ratts Tyerell]] for death in large part due to his cheating methods, although Tyerell never got the opportunity to kill him, ending up getting killed in the [[Laguna Caves/Legends|Laguna Caves]] during the first lap. However, during the last lap, Skywalker caught up with him. After a few attempts to ram his Podracer into Anakin's to knock him off course, their pods tangled with each other. Anakin boosted his engines, sending Sebulba's left engine flying. It hit a rock, went spinning, and then burst into three flaming pieces. His right engine was devastated when it hit the ground and exploded. Sebulba survived without injury, merely cursing in frustration over his defeat.<ref name="Episode 1" />

The loss was a temporary blow to Sebulba's reputation and ego. Sebulba recovered quickly: purchasing [[Anakin Skywalker's Podracer/Legends|Anakin's Podracer]] from [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]], he showed up his rivals at the [[Vinta Harvest Classic/Legends|Vinta Harvest Classic]] and the [[Phoebos Memorial Run/Legends|Phoebos Memorial Run]] race on his home planet of Malastare the following season. Sebulba went on to win many more races, with his brutal competitive edge.<ref name="Star Wars: Republic: Emissaries to Malastare">''[[Star Wars: Emissaries to Malastare]]''</ref>

===Later life===
[[File:Sebulba_malastare.jpg|thumb|left|Sebulba racing on Malastare]]
At some point in 32 BBY, Sebulba had learned that a Dug called [[Gazurga]] had bet against him in the Boonta Eve Classic Podrace. Sebulba considered Gazurga a traitor, and posted a bounty on him of 4,000 credits. This bounty was claimed by [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]].<ref name="BH">''[[Star Wars: Bounty Hunter]]''</ref>

Sebulba, after a while, took a rest and quit Podracing. His son, [[Hekula]], was allowed to fly Sebulba's new Podracer six years after the Boonta Eve Classic, also being beaten by Anakin. Hekula, however, was a rookie and smashed the Podracer in his debut race. Sebulba then purchased a [[Plug-G Gargantua|Plug-G ''Gargantua'']], a remake of his famous podracer that crashed in the Boonta Eve Classic. After purchasing the pod, Sebulba forbade Hekula from Podracing, never letting him near any Podracer or Podrace again.<ref name="Jedi Quest: The Dangerous Games" />

Eight years after Anakin Skywalker had won the Boonta Eve Classic, Sebulba wanted revenge and challenged Anakin one last time to race on his home turf once more, with his newly acquired ''Gargantua''. After Anakin salvaged parts of his Podracer that Hekula crashed, he entered the race. The result of the race is unknown.<ref name="Star Wars: Racer Revenge">''[[Star Wars: Racer Revenge]]''</ref>

Sebulba died by [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].<ref name="Death" />

Sebulba's grandson [[Pugwis]] continued his family's Podracing traditon. He inherited his grandfather's violent temperament, but he lacked the skills of his grandfather and often ended up disqualified. He participated in [[Jabba's demolition games]]<ref name="Demolition">''[[Star Wars: Demolition]]''</ref> in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]] using a Podracer with a design based on his grandfather's.<ref name="NEGTC" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Sebulba_Concept_Art.jpg|thumb|Concept art of Sebulba]]
Sebulba was a completely CGI character, and was played by ''Star Wars'' voice actor [[Lewis MacLeod]] in [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']]. MacLeod reprised his role as Sebulba in the video games ''[[Star Wars: Episode I Racer|Star Wars Episode I: Racer]]'', ''[[Star Wars: Super Bombad Racing]]'', ''[[Star Wars: Racer Revenge]]'', ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Video Game]]'' and ''[[Kinect Star Wars]]''. He also played [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] in [[Star Wars: Obi-Wan (video game)|''Star Wars: Obi-Wan'']], ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'' and ''Star Wars: Super Bombad Racing''.

Early script notes for Sebulba described him as "spidery," and Lucas envisioned a character with a tangle of agile limbs that functioned both as hands and feet. Since he had to operate a Podracer&mdash;and be one of the preeminent pilots in the sport&mdash;he had to be light in frame yet powerful and deadly. Thus came Sebulba's thin yet muscular build. His face was inspired by that of a camel, though early drawings gave him tusks that hindered lip-sync. Sebulba's costume was inspired by medieval armor, and his goggles magnified his eyes to make his appearance even more unsettling.<ref name="DB">{{DB|character|sebulba|Sebulba}}</ref>

Some fans erroneously believe Sebulba makes a cameo appearance in [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Attack of the Clones'']], in an [[Air taxi/Legends|air taxi]] during the speeder chase on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. However, this is actually [[Seboca/Legends|Seboca]]. He can also be seen exiting [[Dex's Diner/Legends|Dex's Diner]] while Obi-Wan Kenobi and [[Dexter Jettster/Legends|Dex]] are talking. Other Dugs appearing in the film include [[Rednax/Legends|Rednax]].

[[File:Sebulba-WSMI.png|thumb|left||A 3D maquette of Sebulba's final design]]
In the bonus features of ''The Phantom Menace'', Sebulba briefly uses a flamethrower in a failed attempt to fry Anakin's pod. The scene was eventually cut.

In the game ''[[Star Wars: Bounty Hunter]]'', two of many secondary bounties on the planet Malastare are Dugs named [[Nebulba]] and [[Xijulba]]. The ID scanner on Jango's helmet shows that they are part of Sebulba's family.

In the video game ''Episode I Racer'' he is a track favorite three times, yet the only way of unlocking this racer and his pod is to complete the galactic circuit with first place on each race of the tournament. Sebulba indeed has the highest top speed in the game without enhancements, topping 600 miles per hour. However, while most racers can boost their speed by 200 to 400 mph, his speed boost thrust adds 185 mph, the second slowest speed boost in the game.

Sebulba also appears in the sequel ''Racer Revenge''. In this game the player plays in Sebulba's new podracer, the ''Gargantua''. His Episode I vehicle, which is faster than his newer podracer, is unlockable by beating the tournament. The game play is radically different, with the inclusion of a new and improved combat system where the player is given a single pod to pilot for the duration of the race. It has a health bar, and when it is depleted the pod crashes and explodes spectacularly. Graphics and handling are also improved, and there are new pilots and tracks.
